digest.top_line: SENOMAC: 5-yr RFS 89.7% vs 88.7%, HR 0.89 (0.66-1.19) — completion ALND omittable after 1-2 SN macromets, with nodal RT in ~89%.
digest.tldr: Breast carried the day's only data. SENOMAC extends axillary de-escalation past Z0011/AMAROS into T3, mastectomy, and extracapsular extension, but the omission is nodal-RT-covered omission (~89% both arms) with no protocol-defined target volume or dose, so the RT field is inherited from national guidelines rather than tested. Primary endpoint is OS and is not reported.

sites.intro: Axillary de-escalation moves into the populations prior trials excluded, on a nodal RT backbone the protocol never specified.

studies.name: SENOMAC
studies.tldr: 5-yr RFS 89.7% vs 88.7%, HR 0.89 (0.66-1.19), noninferior omitting completion ALND after 1-2 SN macromets.
details: 🔍 Phase 3 noninferiority, 67 hospitals in 5 countries, N=2766 enrolled 2015-2021; per-protocol 2540
🔍 Eligibility widened vs prior trials: cN0 T1-T3, mastectomy allowed, extracapsular extension allowed, 1-2 SN macromets (>2mm)
📐 Noninferiority margin: upper CI bound for recurrence-or-death HR had to be <1.44; observed 1.19, P<0.001
📊 Nodal RT in ~89% of both arms (1192/1326 SLNB-only, 1058/1197 dissection); whole-breast RT mandatory after BCS
⚠️ Protocol stipulated NO specific nodal target volumes or doses, so this is 'nodal RT as per national guidelines', not a defined field
📐 RT quality control: 1154 plans reviewed; eCRF matched plan in 99.3% for breast/chest wall, 96.6% for nodal target volumes
📊 pN upstaging in the dissection arm: pN2 in 9.9% and pN3 in 3.0%, vs pN2 0.5% and pN3 0% in the SLNB-only arm
📊 Non-SN metastases found in 403/1167 (34.5%) dissected pts; 31.3% with one SN macromet, 51.3% with two
🔗 vs Z0011 (BCS + whole-breast tangents only) and AMAROS (axillary RT replaced ALND): SENOMAC excluded micromets, allowed T3 and ECE, and enrolled >1/3 mastectomy pts
⚠️ Median f/u 46.8 mo (range 1.5-94.5) in a mostly luminal population that recurs late; 5-yr read is early
⚠️ Primary endpoint is OS (switched from BCSS in 2020) and is NOT reported here; this paper reports the secondary RFS endpoint

verdict.rationale: Prespecified secondary endpoint of a phase 3 noninferiority trial, margin cleared with wide distance; extends Z0011/AMAROS to mastectomy, T3 and ECE rather than contradicting them.
verdict.audience: cN0 T1-T3 breast cancer, 1-2 sentinel-node macrometastases

studies.significance: Nodal RT is the hidden co-intervention: 89.9% and 88.4% of the two arms got regional nodal irradiation, so this is axillary de-escalation ON TOP OF nodal RT, closer to AMAROS/OTOASOR than to Z0011. Target volumes and doses to specific nodal levels are not reported (detailed RT review ongoing), so the field that made omission safe is undefined.
studies.monday_clinic: In cN0 T1-T3 disease with one or two sentinel-node macrometastases who will receive regional nodal irradiation, including after mastectomy or with extracapsular extension, this supports omitting completion axillary dissection; it does not speak to pts who will get no nodal RT, or to 3+ macrometastases.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective randomised **phase 3 noninferiority** trial, 1:1, 67 hospitals in Sweden, Denmark, Germany, Greece and Italy. **Primary endpoint is overall survival** (changed from breast cancer-specific survival in 2020); this report covers the prespecified secondary endpoint of recurrence-free survival. Median follow-up **46.8 months** (range 1.5 to 94.5).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: cN0 **T1 to T3** breast cancer with **one or two sentinel-node macrometastases** (>2 mm); preoperative axillary ultrasound mandatory. Deliberately included groups prior trials excluded: **mastectomy** (36.7% and 35.7%), **extracapsular extension** (about one third), **T3** (5.5% and 6.1%). Median age 61; 87.3% and 85.8% ER-positive HER2-negative.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **No protocol-specified target volumes or doses**; RT followed national guidelines, which in Sweden and Denmark means routine nodal irradiation. Nodal RT reached **1192/1326 (89.9%)** in the SLNB-only group and **1058/1197 (88.4%)** in the dissection group. Whole-breast RT after BCS was mandatory. Source-data verification of 1154 plans showed eCRF-to-plan concordance of 99.3% for breast/chest wall and 96.6% for nodal volumes.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: 5-yr recurrence-free survival **89.7% (87.5-91.9)** vs **88.7% (86.3-91.1)**. Regional recurrence was rare and balanced (6 vs 6). 5-yr OS 92.9% vs 92.0%; 5-yr breast cancer-specific survival 97.1% vs 96.6%. Dissection removed a mean of 15 nodes vs 2 with SLNB alone.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Z0011 enrolled 1999-2004 (BCS only, ~40% micromets, protocol-prohibited nodal RT in 19%) and AMAROS 2001-2010 (only 248 mastectomy pts, ECE not reported). SENOMAC restricts to macromets and adds mastectomy, T3 and ECE. Because nodal irradiation was near-universal, the authors place these results alongside **AMAROS and OTOASOR**, not POSNOC, SINODAR-ONE or Z0011.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents cN0 T1-T3 pts with one or two sentinel-node macrometastases receiving guideline adjuvant systemic therapy and nodal RT, including after mastectomy and with extracapsular extension. Does not represent pts managed without nodal irradiation, those with 3 or more macrometastases, micrometastasis-only disease, or men (only 10 enrolled).

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The **overall survival primary endpoint is not reported here**, and a mostly luminal population recurring late makes a 46.8-month read early. Detailed nodal target-volume and dose data are pending, so the RT that underwrote omission cannot yet be specified. Withdrawal was higher in the dissection arm, reflecting pts' wish to avoid the operation.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The dissection arm's node counts show what omission gives up in staging, not outcome: **pN2 in 9.9% and pN3 in 3.0%** of dissected pts vs 0.5% and 0% with SLNB only, and non-sentinel metastases in **34.5%** overall (51.3% when two sentinel nodes were involved). Occult nodal disease is common and, with systemic therapy plus nodal RT, apparently does not need surgical clearance.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Nodal irradiation was the co-intervention, not a footnote: 89.9% and 88.4% of the arms received it, so omission was tested on top of regional RT and reads with AMAROS and OTOASOR rather than Z0011. Target volumes and doses to specific nodal levels are not reported, with the detailed RT review still ongoing, so the field that made this safe is unspecified.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Systemic therapy was near-universal (about 65% chemotherapy, 93% endocrine, 9% HER2-directed) and assigned by national guidelines, so omission was tested with a modern backbone in place. Losing completion dissection removes the pN2/pN3 information (9.9% and 3.0% of dissected pts) that some regimen decisions have historically leaned on.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Extends axillary omission past the Z0011 fence: mastectomy (36.7%), T3 (5.5%) and extracapsular extension (about a third) all sat inside eligibility, and none of those subgroup HRs excluded 1.00. Completion dissection found non-sentinel disease in 34.5% and upstaged 9.9% to pN2, so the tradeoff is staging information, not recurrence.
